key_insight: SolCloudLLM combines sky images and historical time-series with bidirectional multimodal fusion to improve short-term solar forecasting, especially when clouds cause rapid irradiance and PV ramps.
engineering_relevance: Better cloud-aware forecasting can improve PV dispatch, reserve scheduling, and grid operations while reducing reliance on large site-specific datasets.
method: Align sky-image patches with time-series patches.
Fuse both modalities bidirectionally into a unified representation.
Map the fused embedding into an LLM for forecasting.
evidence_signal: On the SIRTA and SKIPP'D datasets, the method outperformed baselines across all horizons, with up to 25.4% relative MSE reduction and strong few-shot performance.
watch_item: Performance gains appear concentrated in cloudy conditions, so deployment should verify camera quality, site calibration, and robustness when imagery is missing or degraded.
paper_title: Bidirectional Multimodal Fusion of Sky Images and Time-Series for Solar Forecasting with Large Language Models
